analysis.title: Sony Group (6758.T): 2Q beat, as both platforms and content drive earnings growth; ample upside remains, raise GSe and TP, maintain Buy
key_insights: 2Q FY3/27 operating profit from continuing operations was ¥622.3 bn (+45% yoy), against GS estimate ¥510.9 bn and Bloomberg consensus ¥491.1 bn. The beat versus GS was ¥111.4 bn, split ¥38.8 bn G&NS, ¥49.5 bn Pictures and ¥20.8 bn I&SS.

FY3/27 operating profit guidance was raised from ¥1,720 bn to ¥1,870 bn. That is above the previous GS estimate (¥1,757.2 bn) and Bloomberg consensus (¥1,778.9 bn). The ¥150 bn raise comes from G&NS +¥40 bn, Pictures +¥50 bn, Music +¥25 bn and I&SS +¥30 bn, with ET&S unchanged.
GS raises FY3/27-FY3/31 operating profit estimates by +6% to +9%. The drivers are a weaker yen assumption (¥155/USD to ¥160/USD) and higher outlooks for the three entertainment businesses and I&SS.

GS raises the 12-month target price from ¥4,700 to ¥4,800 and maintains Buy. Price is ¥4,211, implying 14.0% upside. The target is an EV/EBITDA sum-of-the-parts valuation on FY3/29E, with a 10% conglomerate discount.

G&NS: segment sales were ¥1,208.5 bn against GS estimate ¥1,013.8 bn. PlayStation MAU reached 127 mn in September (a record for the month), total play time rose 4% yoy, and PS5 sell-in was 2.6 mn units against GS estimate 1.8 mn. Segment margin rose to 18.2% from 15.3% excluding one-off losses.
Sony says it offset memory price increases through promotions, price adjustments and cost cuts, and expects FY3/27 hardware earnings to be flat on FY3/26.
Marvel's Wolverine, released in September, has sold more than 2.4 mn units cumulatively.
God of War Laufey was postponed to 1Q FY3/28 (April-June 2027). This shifts its earnings contribution out of FY3/27, but the G&NS outlook was still raised.

Pictures: segment sales were ¥513.7 bn against GS estimate ¥446 bn. Spider-Man: Brand New Day (released July 31) ranks first all-time in North America and third all-time worldwide at the box office. Related game sales roughly doubled and Sony Music songs in the film passed 1 bn streams. GS raises its FY3/27 Pictures operating profit estimate by 30% and FY3/28 onward by 3%, and still forecasts a yoy profit decline in FY3/28 as the film's effect fades.

I&SS: segment sales were ¥577.6 bn (GS ¥581.6 bn) and operating profit was ¥154.6 bn against GS ¥133.8 bn, helped by forex and cost control. Margin was 26.8% (+4.3 ppt yoy). Sony said the July-September smartphone market fell about 20% yoy on memory market conditions, driven by mid-range and low-end weakness, and that the 1H/2H shipment balance will differ from past years.

The Kumamoto earthquake costs I&SS an annual loss of about ¥16 bn in the new guidance (work-in-progress inventory damage, equipment repairs, lost opportunity). The Kumamoto Technology Center has returned to pre-earthquake operating levels.

Upcoming catalysts: Grand Theft Auto VI (Rockstar, November 19, 2026), Jumanji: Open World theatrical release (December 25, 2026), and God of War Laufey (April-June 2027). Crunchyroll plans a dedicated hub on the PS5 home screen in spring 2027.
GS forecasts: FY3/27E revenue ¥13,233.2 bn, operating profit ¥1,912.4 bn (new) vs ¥1,757.2 bn (old), EPS ¥235.2 vs ¥219.8. FY3/28E operating profit ¥1,992.1 bn and EPS ¥254.4. FY3/27E P/E is 17.9x.
Sony's share price is up 18.1% over 3 months and 34.7% over 6 months, but down 0.8% over 12 months (17.7% behind TOPIX).

market_movers.rationale: Target raised from ¥4,700 to ¥4,800 after a 2Q operating profit beat and a guidance raise. GS sees further upside from PlayStation engagement and profitability, Pictures growth and Crunchyroll.

sector_views.rationale: Buy on Sony as an entertainment company with room to re-rate. Earnings drivers are PS5 monetization, Pictures and Crunchyroll growth, and synergies across IP in games, video and music.

earnings_insights: Sony 2Q FY3/27 (quarter to September 2026, reported): operating profit from continuing operations ¥622.3 bn (+45% yoy) vs GS estimate ¥510.9 bn and Bloomberg consensus ¥491.1 bn.

Sony 2Q FY3/27 reported segment results: G&NS sales ¥1,208.5 bn (GS est ¥1,013.8 bn), Pictures sales ¥513.7 bn (GS est ¥446 bn), I&SS sales ¥577.6 bn (GS est ¥581.6 bn), I&SS operating profit ¥154.6 bn (GS est ¥133.8 bn).
Company FY3/27 operating profit guidance raised from ¥1,720 bn to ¥1,870 bn. Bloomberg consensus before the raise was ¥1,778.9 bn and the previous GS estimate was ¥1,757.2 bn.

GS EPS estimates (forecast): FY3/27E ¥235.2 (old ¥219.8), FY3/28E ¥254.4 (old ¥234.2), FY3/29E ¥250.0 (old ¥226.2). Quarterly EPS: 2Q reported ¥76.8 in the detailed table and ¥75.2 in the summary table, 3Q26E ¥74.0.
Segment guidance for FY3/27 operating profit: G&NS ¥700 bn (from ¥660 bn), Pictures ¥200 bn (from ¥150 bn), Music ¥445 bn (from ¥420 bn), I&SS ¥450 bn (from ¥420 bn), ET&S ¥150 bn unchanged.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS raised its forex assumption from ¥155/USD to ¥160/USD. A weaker yen lifts the yen value of Sony's overseas earnings, mainly in I&SS, and accounts for part of the estimate increase.
Company commentary says the decline came from memory market conditions and was concentrated in mid-range and low-end devices, with the high end falling less.

risk_factors: G&NS: lower PS5 hardware unit sales, lower revenue per console from delayed software or weaker live service and DLC, and weaker hardware profitability from higher promotion expenses or component costs.
Memory price increases are a cost pressure on PlayStation hardware, which Sony has so far offset.
Pictures: slower paid subscriber growth at Crunchyroll or higher promotion and marketing expense. GS also expects a yoy profit decline in FY3/28 as the Spider-Man effect fades.
I&SS: slower CMOS image sensor growth for mobile devices, ASP declines from competition (particularly Chinese companies), or weaker yields as sensors become harder to make.
Sony expects the 1H/2H shipment balance in I&SS to shift because of supply-chain inventory levels and customer product cycles.
